# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 ✋]

I need to figure out what Mute is trying to convey through gestures, and share the bomb's visual info with Blind (via speech, since Blind can hear me).

Let me think about this: Mute can't speak but can gesture to me. Mute knows the manual. Mute is trying to tell me something using gestures — likely mapping symbols to wire colors, actions, or numbers, since gestures have no inherent meaning until we assign it.

The gestures received: [👍 ✌], [👎 ☝], [🖐 ✋] — three pairs, possibly matching my three wires (1,2,3) with some instruction (cut/don't cut), or matching display/light states.

Since this is turn 1, I don't yet know Mute's intended mapping. I should first give Blind and Mute the raw bomb state, so Mute can correlate manual instructions with what I see, and establish a shared code with Mute over time. I'll speak the bomb details to Blind and Mute (both hear me), and ask Mute to use gestures consistently per wire number so we can build a code.

```
speak(text="Deaf here. Bomb shows: display 0, light white, wire 1 yellow, wire 2 green, wire 3 blue. Mute, I see three gesture pairs but don't know their meaning yet. Blind, hold off acting. Mute, please gesture one pair per wire number in order 1,2,3, using thumbs up for cut and thumbs down for do not cut, so I can relay to Blind.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

The light changed from white to purple — that's new information I should relay. Mute now sent three single gestures, likely answering my request: one per wire, in order 1,2,3. 👍 for wire 1 (yellow), 👎 for wire 2 (green), 👎 for wire 3 (blue). That would mean: cut wire 1, don't cut wire 2, don't cut wire 3 — if my proposed convention was understood and adopted.

I should relay this interpretation to Blind, but cautiously since I can't be 100% sure Mute used my exact convention. I'll state my interpretation clearly and ask Mute to confirm/deny via a distinct gesture if I'm wrong, while telling Blind the tentative instruction and the light color change (which might matter per the manual).

```
speak(to="blind", text="Update: light changed from white to purple, display still 0, wires unchanged: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. My reading of Mute's gestures using the convention I proposed: cut wire 1 yellow, do not cut wire 2 green, do not cut wire 3 blue. Wait for Mute to confirm before you act.")
speak(to="mute", text="I read your three gestures as: wire1 cut, wire2 no, wire3 no, matching my proposed convention thumbs up equals cut, thumbs down equals no. If that is correct, gesture a single thumbs up next turn to confirm. If wrong, gesture a single thumbs down to reject and I will propose another way.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute confirmed with a single thumbs up. The light changed again, now to red — this progression (white → purple → red) seems important and I should keep relaying it. The wires and display remain unchanged.

Since Mute confirmed the convention, Blind now has a clear instruction: cut wire 1 (yellow), leave wires 2 and 3 alone. But I should also flag the light color change since it might be a timer/state indicator that changes the required action — I don't know the manual, so I'll just report facts and let Mute/Blind decide via their own logic, while confirming to Blind that Mute confirmed.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute confirmed the reading: cut wire 1 yellow only, leave wire 2 green and wire 3 blue alone. Also note the light is now red, was purple last turn, white before that - display still reads 0. Wires unchanged. Proceed with cutting wire 1 unless Mute signals otherwise.")
speak(to="mute", text="Confirmed received, thank you. Light is now red, changed from purple then white, display still 0. Let me know if this light progression changes the instruction - I will keep watching for changes.")
wait()
```
